newsitem.title: USA: Henkel ups Loctite bid to $61 a share.
newsitem.headline: Henkel ups Loctite bid to $61 a share.

text.p: Henkel KGaA of Germany said Wednesday it raised its offer for the rest of Loctite Corp. to $61 a share, or about $1.3 billion, from its previous offer of $57.75 a share, or about $1.2 billion.
The increased bid is for the 65 percent of Loctite that Henkel does not already own.
A spokesman for Loctite, a Hartford, Conn.-based adhesives maker, said the company had no comment.

A month ago, Henkel raised its initial $56 a share bid and also launched an unwelcome tender offer for Loctite shares. A special committee of Loctite directors called Henkel's initial two bids insufficient.
The revised bid by Henkel, a Dusseldorf-based speciality chemicals company, is subject to execution of a friendly merger agreement and other conditions, the company said.

Last week, Loctite effectively opened the door to all potential bidders by establishing a formal auction process to sell itself. Under that process, Loctite had set a deadline of Wednesday afternoon for offers from interested parties.
While no new bidders have emerged, analysts have said Loctite was scouring the international chemical industry for a "white knight" to counter the Henkel offer.

A Loctite representative and an investment banker met with the chief executive of a potential bidder other than Henkel, Loctite said in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday. It said that Robert Fiondella, chairman of the special committee of Loctite's board, met on Monday with a potential bidder that it did not name.
Based on Loctite's 32 million shares outstanding, the revised Henkel offer is worth about $1.27 billion.
Loctite, which also makes sealants and coatings, earned $84 million, or $2.40 a share, on revenues of $785 million last year.
